listing.name: Banjo-Tooie — XBLA (Banjo Tooie XBLA Recomp)
listing.summary: Documented Windows native source-build route using your own Banjo-Tooie XBLA files. Add only a completed authorized banjotooie.exe build; the packaged outer launcher has a separate process-lifetime hold.

steps.title: Use the documented native source-build route
steps.instruction: Use an authorized completed native source build from the upstream Building from source route, keeping its SDK and third-party notices. This route is distinct from the packaged Banjo-Tooie.exe launcher. Upstream requires CMake 3.25+, Clang 20+, Ninja, and the Windows MSVC/Windows SDK toolchain; its documented x86-64-v3 compiler options require a suitable CPU. The selected tree pins the iron-jay ReXGlue fork as a submodule. Runtime/component licenses remain separate, and the repository does not grant original-game rights. No automated acquisition or rebuild is offered by this guide.

steps.title: Complete original-data extraction and generation with upstream
steps.instruction: Supply your own legally owned Xbox 360 XBLA Banjo-Tooie package, not an N64 ROM. Deliberately finish upstream extraction outside Portcove, preserving default.xex and the expected extracted files and RAWFiles layout. The source manifest uses ../xbla/files/default.xex and includes overrides.toml. Its generated source and generated/rexglue.cmake are intentionally absent from Git: finish the pinned SDK codegen against that manifest before the documented CMake configure/build target banjotooie. The SDK codegen creates the missing helper after successful generation. Do not point Portcove at an incomplete clone, run a generator through Play, or infer original authenticity from upstream extraction, which does not verify container signatures/hashes.

steps.title: Add only the completed native game executable
steps.instruction: Select the completed banjotooie.exe build with its containing output folder as the working folder, retaining rexruntime.dll and every companion staged by the build. Set the two launch arguments --game_data_root and the absolute path to your own extracted XBLA game-data directory, preserving the path as one argument. The selected native app owns its Windows message loop and waits for the guest game; it is a different entry from the outer Banjo-Tooie.exe launcher. That packaged launcher starts a child then exits, so do not use it for a tracked Portcove session or select a private PyInstaller extraction path. Saving launch details and Play are separate actions.

steps.title: Preserve the direct build’s actual player-data roots
steps.instruction: Upstream/player owns runtime replacement and the extracted originals. For this direct native app the default player-data root is Documents/banjotooie and its cache is under that root; the executable-side banjotooie.toml is separate. Explicit --user_data_root, --cache_path or opt-in --update_data_root values select other roots. Retain the exact chosen arguments and preserve all active roots before changing builds. The packaged launcher’s BanjoTooie-Data/saves override is a different layout and is not automatically inherited or migrated by a direct build. Portcove does not promise external-save backup, rollback, compatibility or deletion.

warnings: This is a conditional, source-inspected native-build guide. No original data, generation, compilation, prepared output, native game, real save, complete dependency ABI, artifact integrity or source-to-binary correspondence was inspected or executed. The Windows packaged-launcher lifetime hold remains; source/component acquisition rights require their own applicable authorization.
